craft_claim: Direct verbal (and bodily) address intensifies parasocial interaction, so second-person address and conversational turn-taking make a written voice read as a companion.

supporting_evidence.note: Introduces para-social interaction: the perceived face-to-face relationship with a performer, sustained across repeated contact as a one-sided bond.
Viewers reported more intense parasocial experience when addressed on both bodily and verbal levels; perspective-taking and perceived attractiveness strengthened the effect.
Basho writes a companionable travel account addressed to readers as fellow travellers, sustaining intimacy at a distance without face-to-face contact.

counterevidence.note: The effect is per-contact and enhanced by perceived attractiveness; repeated or unearned address is not guaranteed to deepen the parasocial bond.

scope: Blog, essay, broadcast, newsletter, epistolary and marketing copy where a speaking persona is present.
exceptions: Imp personal or academic registers where direct address would breach expected distance.
Forms with no persona (reference works, legal text).
